title: Pick Up Where You Left Off: An Efficient Solution for Continuous Vector Similarity Search

problem.claim: Real-time AI applications need efficient vector similarity search for continuous query streams whose queries exhibit continuity and correlation.

gap.claim: Existing methods are optimized for isolated queries, while prior-result reuse either sacrifices accuracy through semantic caching or provides only marginal efficiency gains.

contributions.claim: The paper formalizes Continuous Vector Similarity Search (CVSS).
Reuse is an end-to-end framework that decomposes CVSS into a Reuse Trigger for deciding when to reuse prior results and a Reuse Searcher for determining how to reuse them effectively.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the two Reuse components significantly reduce redundant computation while maintaining near-identical recall.
The authors report extensive experiments on four real-world datasets.
The authors report that Reuse achieves 1.6--3.0× higher throughput in QPS than state-of-the-art methods at the same recall.

narrative_sequence.summary: Efficient vector similarity search is important for RAG and other real-time AI applications.
Existing search methods do not exploit continuity and correlation in real-world query streams.
The paper defines this setting as Continuous Vector Similarity Search.
Reuse addresses CVSS with coordinated components for deciding when and how to reuse prior search results.
The authors report reduced redundant computation, near-identical recall, and higher throughput across four datasets.

source_observation.claim: Query streams can contain continuity and correlation that isolated-query search methods fail to exploit.

interpretation.claim: For sequential workloads, treating each query independently may leave reusable computation untapped.

application.claim: Systems serving multi-turn dialogue or multi-hop question answering may benefit from explicit mechanisms for deciding when and how to reuse prior search results.

exception.claim: Reuse should preserve recall because semantic caching can sacrifice accuracy.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the four datasets, baselines, hardware, or experimental protocol.
The abstract does not describe the recall metric, latency trade-offs, or conditions behind the throughput range.
The abstract does not provide implementation details for the Reuse Trigger or Reuse Searcher.
